operator_rule: A consumer may treat 'stale' as a blocking condition ONLY if it controls the two caller-owned axes below (canonical publication and a stable generated_at). If it does not, its stale check will fire on every refresh and it must not claim the check is meaningful. Deriving generated_at from repository content -- the commit timestamp of the registry, or the registry's own source_sha256 mapped to a fixed instant -- is the supported way to hold that axis stable; wall-clock is not.
summary: WWW's Slice 5 must block closure on a stale provider fingerprint. That is only safe if 'stale' means 'the resolved knowledge actually changed' and never merely 'this ran somewhere else'. These four cases make the distinction mechanically decidable. The recorded baseline fingerprint below is pinned RAW: it reproduces byte-identically from a different scratch root with the global vault mounted at a different absolute path, which is precisely the property that was NOT true when this pack was first frozen and is true now.
